brief: Citadel Securities strategist Scott Rubner remains constructive on US equities long term but flags a shift in near-term asymmetry: he calls September a tactical downside window, not a change in the broader bullish trend. The August rally's supports are fading. Earnings are largely reported (93% of S&P 500 weight, 88% beating by a median 7%), leaving a lighter corporate calendar. Retail buying and corporate buybacks both seasonally slow in September, with buyback blackout windows accelerating around September 12. Systematic strategies (CTA, vol-control, risk-parity) have already redeployed most of the capacity created by the July deleveraging reset, leaving less room for further buying, while quarter-end pension rebalancing (funding at 112%, the highest since 2001) may favor bond buying over equities. Meanwhile downside protection is unusually cheap (SPX skew near its first percentile, VIX at 14.4), roughly $6.2 trillion of options notional expires September 18, and the catalyst calendar turns to macro data (NFP, PPI, CPI, FOMC) during history's weakest seasonal month, worse in midterm-election years. Conclusion: use strength now to reduce exposure and add inexpensive protection, expecting a possible better entry and more constructive setup around mid-October.
